study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the Physicians' Health Study
reason: Baseline plasma samples preceded the development of prostate cancer, establishing prospective incident general prostate cancer analysis. No aggressive prostate cancer subtype is analyzed. A literal total analytic sample size is not reported; the abstract separately reports 120 cases and 120 controls.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The RR for eating red meat at least five times per week compared with less than once a week was 2.5 (95% CI = 0.9-6.7) and was little changed by adjustment for alpha-linolenic acid, although alpha-linolenic acid levels were correlated with intake of red meat and butter.
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate concerns the risk of overall incident prostate cancer and has no aggressive-disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: For linoleic acid, RRs in successively higher quartiles were 0.7 (95% CI = 0.4-1.5), 0.8 (95% CI = 0.4-1.6), and 0.6 (95% CI = 0.3-1.3), with the lowest quartile as referent (P trend = .24).
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported linoleic-acid estimates concern overall incident prostate cancer, not an aggressive subtype.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The relative risks (RRs) of prostate cancer for men in successively higher quartiles of plasma alpha-linolenic acid level were 3.0 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.2-7.3), 3.4 (95% CI = 1.6-7.5), and 2.1 (95% CI = 0.9-4.9), compared with those with levels below the detection threshold (P trend = .03).
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported alpha-linolenic-acid estimates concern overall incident prostate cancer, not an aggressive subtype.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
